tools.name: Read

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context...

behaviours: file_path must be absolute.
Reads up to 2000 lines by default (binary constant Z$t=2000; prompt 'Reads up to ${Z$t} lines by default').

Output in cat -n format, line numbers start at 1: 'Each line is the line number, a single separator (a tab or `:`), then the verbatim file content (including any leading whitespace).' Observed in this session: number right-aligned (6 wide) then a tab.

One call returns at most 25,000 tokens (CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS); a whole file over the token cap returns the first page with a 'PARTIAL view' notice; a whole file over 256 KB, or an offset/limit read over the cap, returns an error telling it to page or Grep. allow_large (v2.1.296+) sizes the read to remaining context.

Images (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP) returned as visual content (resized; refuses > 128 MB); PDFs read whole when short, `pages` required for > 10 pages, max 20 pages/call, page rendering needs pdftoppm; .ipynb returns all cells with outputs (error over 256 KB of cells; refuses > 100 MB).
Empty file -> notice; offset past end -> notice with line count; directories are not readable (use ls); binary extensions (.xlsx, .zip, ...) refused.
Per-line truncation: older Claude Code prompts said lines over 2000 chars are truncated; that sentence is NOT in the 2.1.306 binary or docs - NOT CONFIRMED for this version.
Read results are deduplicated: a repeat read of an unchanged file can return type 'file_unchanged' (SDK output type).

workdir.description: Working directory for the command. Defaults to the turn cwd.

tty.description: True allocates a PTY for the command; false or omitted uses plain pipes.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding output. Defaults to 10000 ms; effective range is 250-30000 ms. (Windows text: 'Maximum time to wait before returning a session ID for a still-running command... Effective range on Windows is 10000-30000 ms.')

max_output_tokens.description: Output token budget. Defaults to 10000 tokens; larger requests may be capped by policy.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: The `apply_patch` tool can be used to edit files. This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON.
behaviours: Grammar above is codex-rs/core/assets/tools/apply_patch.lark at rust-v0.157.0, sent verbatim as the freeform tool's `format.definition` (type 'grammar', syntax 'lark').

Multi-environment sessions: the grammar's start rule is rewritten to `start: begin_patch environment_id? hunk+ end_patch` with `environment_id: "*** Environment ID: " filename LF` (apply_patch_spec.rs).

Envelope: first line must be exactly '*** Begin Patch', last line '*** End Patch' (after trim). Errors: "The first line of the patch must be '*** Begin Patch'" / "The last line of the patch must be '*** End Patch'" (parser.rs).

Lenient mode is always on (PARSE_IN_STRICT_MODE=false): leading/trailing whitespace around markers is tolerated, and a patch wrapped in a heredoc (`<<EOF`, `<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"` first line, last line ending in `EOF`, >= 4 lines) is unwrapped.

Hunks: '*** Add File: <path>' followed by one or more '+' lines (file contents = those lines, each newline-terminated); '*** Delete File: <path>'; '*** Update File: <path>' optionally followed by '*** Move to: <new path>' then change chunks.

Update chunk: optional '@@' or '@@ <context line>' header, then lines starting with ' ' (context, kept), '-' (removed), '+' (added); optional '*** End of File' marks a chunk that must match at the end of the file. The first chunk of an update hunk may omit the '@@' header. A bare empty line inside an update hunk is treated as an empty context line.

Errors: an Update hunk with no chunks -> "Update file hunk for path '

' is empty"; unknown header -> "'' is not a valid hunk header. Valid hunk headers: '*** Add File: {path}', '*** Delete File: {path}', '*** Update File: {path}'"; bad chunk line -> "Unexpected line found in update hunk: ''. Every line should start with ' ' (context line), '+' (added line), or '-' (removed line)".
Paths: relative paths resolve against the turn cwd; absolute paths are also accepted (test_parse_patch_accepts_relative_and_absolute_hunk_paths).

Applying an update (file_update.rs compute_replacements): chunks are applied in order with a moving cursor. If a chunk has an '@@ <ctx>' header, the single ctx line is located first (seek_sequence) and the cursor moves past it; failure -> "Failed to find context '<ctx>' in <path>". Then the chunk's old lines (context + '-' lines) are located at or after the cursor; failure -> "Failed to find expected lines in <path>:\n<old lines>". A chunk with no old lines (pure insertion) appends at end of file. If old lines end with an empty line and are not found, the search retries without that trailing empty line.

Line matching (seek_sequence.rs) tries, in order: exact; ignoring trailing whitespace; ignoring leading+trailing whitespace; then after normalizing Unicode dashes/quotes/odd spaces to ASCII. With '*** End of File' the search starts at the end of the file.

Line endings: default mode NormalizeToLf (updated file rewritten with LF and a trailing newline). Feature apply_patch_preserve_line_endings (under development) / env CODEX_APPLY_PATCH_PRESERVE_LINE_ENDINGS=1 keeps original endings and context lines byte-for-byte.

Success output (lib.rs print_summary): 'Success. Updated the following files:' then one line per path: 'A <path>' (added), 'M <path>' (modified), 'D <path>' (deleted). Parse/verify failures are returned to the model as 'apply_patch verification failed: <error>'.

Shell interception: an exec_command whose command is an apply_patch invocation (e.g. `apply_patch <<'EOF' ... EOF`) is intercepted and applied through the same verified path (handlers/apply_patch.rs intercept_apply_patch).

The base system prompt tells the model: use the `apply_patch` tool (never `applypatch`/`apply-patch`), and do not re-read files after apply_patch because the call fails if it did not work (protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md).

codex.apply_patch_grammar:
start: begin_patch hunk+ end_patch
begin_patch: "*** Begin Patch" LF
end_patch: "*** End Patch" LF?

hunk: add_hunk | delete_hunk | update_hunk
add_hunk: "*** Add File: " filename LF add_line+
delete_hunk: "*** Delete File: " filename LF
update_hunk: "*** Update File: " filename LF change_move? change?

filename: /(.+)/
add_line: "+" /(.*)/ LF -> line

change_move: "*** Move to: " filename LF
change: (change_context | change_line)+ eof_line?
change_context: ("@@" | "@@ " /(.+)/) LF
change_line: ("+" | "-" | " ") /(.*)/ LF
eof_line: "*** End of File" LF

%import common.LF
apply_patch_rules: Grammar above is codex-rs/core/assets/tools/apply_patch.lark at rust-v0.157.0, sent verbatim as the freeform tool's `format.definition` (type 'grammar', syntax 'lark').

Multi-environment sessions: the grammar's start rule is rewritten to `start: begin_patch environment_id? hunk+ end_patch` with `environment_id: "*** Environment ID: " filename LF` (apply_patch_spec.rs).

Envelope: first line must be exactly '*** Begin Patch', last line '*** End Patch' (after trim). Errors: "The first line of the patch must be '*** Begin Patch'" / "The last line of the patch must be '*** End Patch'" (parser.rs).

Lenient mode is always on (PARSE_IN_STRICT_MODE=false): leading/trailing whitespace around markers is tolerated, and a patch wrapped in a heredoc (`<<EOF`, `<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"` first line, last line ending in `EOF`, >= 4 lines) is unwrapped.

Hunks: '*** Add File: <path>' followed by one or more '+' lines (file contents = those lines, each newline-terminated); '*** Delete File: <path>'; '*** Update File: <path>' optionally followed by '*** Move to: <new path>' then change chunks.

Update chunk: optional '@@' or '@@ <context line>' header, then lines starting with ' ' (context, kept), '-' (removed), '+' (added); optional '*** End of File' marks a chunk that must match at the end of the file. The first chunk of an update hunk may omit the '@@' header. A bare empty line inside an update hunk is treated as an empty context line.

Errors: an Update hunk with no chunks -> "Update file hunk for path '

' is empty"; unknown header -> "'' is not a valid hunk header. Valid hunk headers: '*** Add File: {path}', '*** Delete File: {path}', '*** Update File: {path}'"; bad chunk line -> "Unexpected line found in update hunk: ''. Every line should start with ' ' (context line), '+' (added line), or '-' (removed line)".
Paths: relative paths resolve against the turn cwd; absolute paths are also accepted (test_parse_patch_accepts_relative_and_absolute_hunk_paths).

Applying an update (file_update.rs compute_replacements): chunks are applied in order with a moving cursor. If a chunk has an '@@ <ctx>' header, the single ctx line is located first (seek_sequence) and the cursor moves past it; failure -> "Failed to find context '<ctx>' in <path>". Then the chunk's old lines (context + '-' lines) are located at or after the cursor; failure -> "Failed to find expected lines in <path>:\n<old lines>". A chunk with no old lines (pure insertion) appends at end of file. If old lines end with an empty line and are not found, the search retries without that trailing empty line.

Line matching (seek_sequence.rs) tries, in order: exact; ignoring trailing whitespace; ignoring leading+trailing whitespace; then after normalizing Unicode dashes/quotes/odd spaces to ASCII. With '*** End of File' the search starts at the end of the file.

Line endings: default mode NormalizeToLf (updated file rewritten with LF and a trailing newline). Feature apply_patch_preserve_line_endings (under development) / env CODEX_APPLY_PATCH_PRESERVE_LINE_ENDINGS=1 keeps original endings and context lines byte-for-byte.

Success output (lib.rs print_summary): 'Success. Updated the following files:' then one line per path: 'A <path>' (added), 'M <path>' (modified), 'D <path>' (deleted). Parse/verify failures are returned to the model as 'apply_patch verification failed: <error>'.

Shell interception: an exec_command whose command is an apply_patch invocation (e.g. `apply_patch <<'EOF' ... EOF`) is intercepted and applied through the same verified path (handlers/apply_patch.rs intercept_apply_patch).

The base system prompt tells the model: use the `apply_patch` tool (never `applypatch`/`apply-patch`), and do not re-read files after apply_patch because the call fails if it did not work (protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md).
codex.apply_patch_example:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: path/add.py
+abc
+def
*** Delete File: path/delete.py
*** Update File: path/update.py
*** Move to: path/update2.py
@@ def f():
-    pass
+    return 123
*** End Patch
